title: Adaptive patterns: usage gallery and migration playbook for tokens, controls, tables, charts
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a compact, example-driven gallery + migration playbook that helps product teams move from legacy token sets and ad-hoc control implementations to the new adaptive design primitives. Scope covers: token usage recommendations (color, spacing, type), primary/secondary/ghost button patterns, accessible table patterns with paging/virtualization notes, and chart embedding guidance for our chart primitives. Output should be a set of 10–15 copy+code examples, migration checklist per component family, do/don't snippets, and a short rollout plan for the docs site (confluence + docs site + storybook).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Publish a gallery page with at least 12 vetted examples covering tokens, buttons, tables, and charts
A2: Provide per-component migration checklists that include common anti-patterns and recommended replacements
A3: Include copy+code snippets compatible with the vNext component API and Storybook playground
A4: Docs reviewed and approved by Eng and PM (signoffs recorded in comments)
A5: Documentation page deployed to staging docs site and linked from the Design System hub
tasks: Audit existing docs and storybook stories for tokens/buttons/tables/charts (task owner: Lena)
Draft usage gallery examples (owner: Ava) — 3 tokens, 4 controls, 3 table patterns, 2 chart embed examples
Write migration checklists and add quick-fix code snippets (owner: Design writers)
Coordinate API compatibility notes with ENG runtime and SDK owners (PR-link in comments)
Add accessibility notes and automated test pointers for each example
Staging deploy and smoke test the docs site, capture screenshots for the rollout announcement
notes: This ticket consolidates scattered guidance into a compact, actionable artifact. Focus on making examples copy-paste friendly and minimizing cognitive load for engineers migrating existing pages. Avoid large API changes — this is doc-facing and migration guidance only.
